runs.model_description: The model ingests raw 100x3 accelerometer windows and constructs a 10-channel feature map inside the graph comprising standardized signals, gravity-centered signals, padded first-difference jerk proxies, and L1 magnitudes. These features are processed through an in-graph dual-branch ensemble with distinct temporal kernel sizes (k=3 for impulses, k=5 for sweeps) utilizing strided Conv2D downsampling and hybrid max/average pooling. The logits from both compact branches are averaged using explicit TFLM-supported arithmetic ops (`ADD` and `MUL`) before a final softmax layer.

runs.improvements: ['Replacing the single-branch network with a dual-branch ensemble (k=3 and k=5) boosted validation F1 macro from 0.8296 to 0.9552 and test F1 macro to 1.0.', 'Adding a third strided Conv2D layer per branch and tuning filter widths to [12, 16, 24] significantly reduced fine-grained class confusion, elevating worst-class recall from 0.6667 to 0.7778 on validation and 1.0 on test.', 'Increasing augmentation depth from 8 to 12 physical variations per sample enhanced model generalization on unseen physical executions.', 'Model flatbuffer size increased from 14.58 KB to 21.84 KB and MFLOPs grew from 0.1913 to 0.2692, remaining comfortably beneath hard device limits while dramatically boosting prediction quality.']

It processes signals through a stem 2D convolution across all sensor axes followed by two depthwise-separable 1D temporal conv blocks with equal strides. Concatenated global max and average pooling outputs are then passed through a soft-max dense layer to classify 10 gesture categories.
runs.key_aspects: Used depthwise-separable convolutions to reduce parameter count to 2.35k and MFLOPs to 0.074. Integrated in-graph normalization to meet deploy contract requirements without external pre-processing. Combined global max and global average pooling to capture both transient peak motions and sustained gesture energy. Enforced equal 2D strides (2, 2) on DepthwiseConv2D layers to overcome TFLite CPU runtime limitations while downsampling time. Applied physical data augmentation and synthetic Null hard-negative generation to eliminate background false triggers.
runs.improvements: This solution represents Cycle 0 baseline execution, achieving perfect 1.0 macro F1 and 1.0 worst-class recall on the unseen frozen test set. Fully quantized int8 model size achieved 11.14 KB, well under the 24 KB soft budget. Peak activation memory (arena) was kept minimal at 2.58 KB against a 16 KB threshold. runs.risks: Validation worst-class recall drops to 0.7778 on validation splits compared to 1.0 on test, indicating vulnerability to small dataset partitioning. Significant headroom remains under the 24 KB size budget, suggesting potential under-capacity for more complex distribution shifts.

runs.model_description: The model consumes a raw 100x3 accelerometer window, applying in-graph normalization followed by a fused Lambda block that constructs 7 feature channels (3 standardized raw, 3 window-centered dynamic motion, and 1 L1 dynamic magnitude). The tensor is reshaped to (100, 1, 7) and processed by a strided stem Conv2D layer and two depthwise-separable Conv2D blocks with equal 2D strides (2, 2) to downsample time. Concatenated global average and max pooling features are passed through a dropout layer and a dense head to yield 10 class predictions, fully converted to Int8 TFLite.
runs.key_aspects: Fused in-graph kinematic processing computes mean-centered motion and dynamic L1 magnitude strictly using allowed primitive TFLM ops (MEAN, SUB, ABS, CONCATENATION). Depthwise-separable Conv2D layers with equal strides (2, 2) downsample temporal length from 100 to 13 while keeping total parameters at 2.6k and estimated MCU latency at 11.25 ms. Concatenation of global average pooling and global max pooling captures both sustained gesture energy and sharp impulse peaks without adding dense layer overhead. Custom multi-modal Null hard negative generation (3D tilted static poses, wrist drift, partial quiet tails, and chunk shuffling) prevents false triggers on resting and background motion. Full-integer Int8 post-training quantization with representative calibration data achieves 100% Int8 kernel execution and perfect agreement with the Keras model.
runs.improvements: Added a fused 7-channel in-graph kinematic layer (mean-centered dynamic motion and L1 dynamic magnitude), providing explicit gravity-removed motion representations. Expanded training distribution with dedicated multi-modal Null hard negatives (tilted static poses, partial window tails, chunk-shuffled segments) and increased augmentation reps from 8 to 12. Validation worst-class recall improved dramatically from 0.5556 to 0.7778, resolving fine-grained confusion among hard gesture pairs. Overall validation score rose from 0.8416 to 0.8568, culminating in perfect 1.0 macro F1, 1.0 worst-class recall, and 0.9153 overall score on the frozen test set.
runs.risks: MFLOPs increased from 0.0724 to 0.1080 and estimated peak activation arena grew from 2.58 KB to 3.22 KB due to the wider 7-channel input tensor in early layers. Estimated MCU latency increased from 7.54 ms to 11.25 ms, though it remains well within the 50 ms budget limit. The small validation split size creates metric sensitivity where a single misclassified sample significantly shifts worst-class recall.
runs.next_experiments: Add first-difference jerk channels (proxy for acceleration changes) to the fused in-graph kinematic block to better separate sharp impact gestures like Slap from Flick. Replace full global pooling with coarse 2-bin temporal segment pooling prior to global aggregation to preserve sequential timing structure for multi-stage gestures like Drop. Introduce a multi-scale dual-branch convolution layer (localized k=3 and temporal k=5) in the feature extractor to concurrently capture brief impulses and longer oscillatory movements.

runs.model_description: The model standardizes 100x3 raw accelerometer windows using an in-graph normalization layer and reshapes them to (100, 1, 3). It passes inputs through a strided 2D Conv stem and two depthwise-separable blocks with (2, 2) strides to reduce temporal length to 13 frames across 20 channels. A 2-segment overlapping Average+Max pooling layer (pool size 7, stride 6) preserves temporal chronology before flattening into an 80-unit feature vector for a 10-class Dense softmax head.
runs.key_aspects: 2-Segment Overlapping Temporal Pooling partitions the 13-frame feature map into overlapping halves (frames 0..6 and 6..12) to retain first-half vs. second-half gesture timing (e.g., free-fall vs. impact in Drop). Channel Projection to 20 filters before pooling keeps the flattened representation compact (80 units), capping Dense parameters at 810 and overall model size at ~10.8 KB. Dual-Teacher Distillation combines predictions from a wide global-pooling teacher and a wide temporal-pooling teacher to train the compact student with zero micro-controller cost. Physics-preserving augmentation separates static gravity vectors from dynamic impulses to warp, rotate, and scale motion while keeping resting poses realistic. Peak-aligned within-class blending aligns same-class sample dynamic energy peaks before mixing to create realistic intermediate training examples.
runs.improvements: Validation macro F1 improved from 0.9120 to 0.9342 and worst-class recall increased from 0.7778 to 0.8889, reaching 1.00 on the frozen test set. Switching to overlapping 2-segment temporal pooling (pool size 7, stride 6) replaced coarse non-overlapping pooling, providing better temporal resolution for sequential gestures. Integrating a dual-teacher distillation framework (soft-target learning) provided smoother decision boundaries, addressing fine-grained class confusion. Although parameter count increased from 1.52k to 2.21k (10.88 KB vs 8.63 KB) and estimated MCU latency rose from 4.01 ms to 6.95 ms, the model remains well within all soft budget limits.
runs.risks: Computational cost increased significantly (0.0667 MFLOPs vs 0.0385 MFLOPs in baseline), nearly doubling estimated MCU execution time. Small validation sample size creates potential metric variance where one misclassified validation sample shifts recall metrics considerably. Quantization representative data calibration requires careful matching with physical augmentations to avoid activation clipping on high-g impact gestures.
runs.next_experiments: Inject an in-graph kinematic feature block (first-difference jerk and L1 magnitude) before the stem Conv2D to improve separation of sharp impulses (Slap vs Poke). Evaluate 3-segment temporal pooling with lower channel count (e.g., 16 channels) to capture three distinct temporal phases (start, peak, rebound) at similar MFLOPs. Adjust distillation weighting toward the temporal teacher (e.g., 0.7 temporal / 0.3 global) to enforce stricter chronological feature learning in the student model.
